draft.emotion: a deliberate and focused moment of turning your attention toward something
notes: Takes the preposition إِلَى (ilā) to mean 'to look at', and فِي (fī) to mean 'to look into / consider'.
Imperfect form: يَنْظُرُ (yanẓuru). Do not confuse with رَأَى (raʾā, 'to see') or شَاهَدَ (šāhada, 'to watch').

senses.definition: To direct your eyes toward someone or something.

examples.translation: The student looked at the board.
examples.emotion: attentive and studious, focused on the lesson

senses.definition: To examine or think carefully about a matter or issue.

examples.translation: We will look into this problem tomorrow.

draftBefore.emotion: a deliberate and focused moment of turning your attention toward something
notes: In Arabic, to say 'to look AT something', you must use the preposition 'إِلَى' (ila) after the verb, as in 'نَظَرَ إِلَى'.
Do not confuse this with 'رَأَى' (ra'a), which means 'to see' or 'to perceive' without necessarily directing one's gaze intentionally.

senses.definition: To turn your eyes and attention toward someone or something to see them clearly.

examples.translation: The student looked at the board.
examples.emotion: attentive and studious, focused on the lesson

senses.definition: To observe or watch something over a period of time.

examples.translation: The father watched his children playing.
examples.emotion: warm and watchful, feeling protective and content
